subject: [RFC PATCH 3/4] memcg_ext: allow BPF to defer memory.high enforcement

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the gfp_mask does not account for task restrictions, which could lead to __GFP_FS and other flags being present when setting up the scan_control instance, potentially causing issues.

Reviewer noted that the gfp_mask passed to BPF may include flags like __GFP_FS and __GFP_IO, which are later cleared when setting up scan_control instance, potentially leading to inconsistent memory allocation behavior.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Sep 24, 2026 at 01:14:59PM -0700, JP Kobryn wrote:
[...]

---

I am passing the same gfp_mask which has been passed to try_charge_memcg(), so
it should be same as what reclaim_high (reclaim internal) sees.

2026-09-24.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where BPF programs are not aware of task restrictions on memory allocation, which can lead to unexpected behavior when enforcing memory.high limits. The patch aims to allow BPF to defer enforcement until after the scan_control instance is set up, ensuring that task restrictions are properly accounted for.
